prerequisites: Average programming skills in a high-level programming language

learning_outcomes.text: To use the knowledge related to programming, mathematics, engineering and technology and has the skills to use them to create complex information technology systems.
To use integrated development environments for creating large complex applications.
To present and explain methods, algorithms, paradigms and techniques used in various branches of computer science.
Identify complex problems and examine related issues to develop solving options and implement solutions.
Combine diverse information to formulate solutions and generate ideas for developing new products and applications.
Present and explain methods, algorithms, paradigms and techniques used in various branches of computer science.
Solutions and generate ideas for developing new products and applications.
GUI applications using architectural templates suitable for specific user interaction applications.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to AI: History, Method, and Ethical Issues; Mathematical Prerequisites; Data Preprocessing.
Machine learning and decision trees.
Neural networks I: Perceptron model, feed-forward neural networks.
Neural networks II: Multi-layer neural networks, backpropagation algorithm.
Types of ANNs I: CNNs, RNNs, LSTMs, GRUs, Transformers, and BERT.
Problem solving as search: problem spaces, uninformed search, BFS, DFS, limited DFS, iterative deepening search, and UCS.
Problem solving as search: informed search, heuristic search, best-first search, Greedy, A* algorithm, and A* variants.
Local search: simulated annealing, hill climbing, and evolutionary computation.
Evolutionary strategies, evolutionary programming, and genetic programming.
Swarm intelligence: particle swarm optimization, ant colony optimization.
Adversarial Searching: Game playing, Minimax search, Alpha-beta pruning.
Intelligent Systems: Support Vector Machines, K-means.
Knowledge representation and reasoning in rule-based systems.
Uncertainty management in rule-based systems.
Get familiar with Scify, Matplotlib, and other packages. Perform data preprocessing.
Monte Carlo Methods: simulation, sampling, and biases.
Build a DT for a specific problem. Validate the results.
Get familiar with PyTorch. Build a perceptron for several problems.
Build and train a simple feedforward artificial network for a specific problem. Select, modify, and visualize specific network parameters.
Solve a classification problem using ANNs.
Build a CNN for image recognition.
Perform transfer learning on a neural network.
Modeling problems for the DFS approach.
Implement an evolutionary algorithm and apply it to a specific problem.
Implement a PSO for a mathematical problem.
Implement an RBS in an uncertain environment.
Hyperheuristics.

assessment_methods.method: Evaluation of laboratory assignments and projects

assessment_rules: All laboratory classes are mandatory, with a minimum attendance requirement of 90% in laboratories. To pass, students need a minimum final mark of 5 (on a scale of 1 to 10).
